en.headline: Experts call for safety-by-design to cut construction fatalities
en.dek: Industry leaders urge embedding safety into building plans after 15 fatal industrial accidents were recorded so far this year.
body: Construction industry leaders have called for safety design to be made a mandatory part of all building development plans, following 15 fatal industrial accidents recorded in Hong Kong so far this year.

Construction Industry Council chairman Thomas Ho On-sing warned that the number of fatalities was rising despite stiffer penalties, saying a genuine safety culture had yet to take root. He estimated that 70 to 80 per cent of worksite accidents stemmed from bad habits and poor mindsets, with pressure to finish projects quickly a major factor in all 15 deaths.

Chau Sze-kit, chairman of the Hong Kong Construction Industry Employees General Union, said safety awareness had improved but the “rushing culture” remained prevalent. He cited recent cases of workers on exterior scaffolding without proper safety belts or independent lifelines.

The comments came during Construction Safety Week 2026, which opened on Monday. Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn noted that overall accident rates fell about 20 per cent between 2023 and 2025 after wider adoption of the Smart Site Safety System, now installed at roughly 80 per cent of local sites.

zh.headline: 業界促將安全設計納入建築規劃減致命意外
zh.dek: 建造業今年已錄得15宗致命工業意外，業界領袖呼籲從設計階段納入安全考慮。
body: 建造業議會主席何安誠及工會代表指出，本港今年至今已錄得15宗致命工業意外，呼籲將安全設計列為所有建築發展計劃的必要部分。
何安誠表示，即使罰則已加重，死亡數字仍上升，反映安全文化尚未真正落地。他估計七至八成工地意外由不良心態及壞習慣造成，而趕工壓力是15宗死亡事故的共同因素。
香港建造業總工會主席周思傑指，安全意識有所提升，但「趕工文化」仍然普遍，近期仍有工人在外牆棚架工作時未正確使用安全帶或獨立救生繩。
言論發表於「建造業安全周2026」期間。發展局局長甯漢豪指出，廣泛採用「安全智慧工地」系統後，建造業整體意外率在2023至2025年間下降約兩成，目前約八成本地工地已安裝該系統。
